notes:
Two fixes, one of which could cost you a licence seat.

**A retry on activation could spend a second seat.** When Docket activates a licence it asks the vendor once, and if that request failed with a server error it asked again — up to four times. But a 500, 502 or 504 can mean the vendor *did* record the activation and only lost the reply on the way back, so asking again could use a second seat off a three-seat key. The code already refused to retry a read timeout on that endpoint for exactly this reason, and said so in its own documentation three paragraphs above the line that retried anyway.

Retrying is now decided by which endpoint is being called, not by the status code. A 429 or 503 is still retried everywhere, because both prove the request never reached the thing that would act on it — that matters, because refusing them would bring back the bug where a busy load balancer got a paying customer told their key was bad. Anything else is retried only where a repeat cannot spend anything.

The other half is what the app says. After an activation it could not confirm, it now tells you not to enter your key again yet, because it may already have activated — instead of a message that invites the one action that spends the second seat.

**Pages dated with `TechArticle` were reported as having no dates.** The check that looks for machine-readable dates matched four schema.org type names — Article, BlogPosting, WebPage and NewsArticle — so a site typing its pages TechArticle, HowTo, Recipe, ScholarlyArticle or Report was told "41 of 41 pages publish no ISO 8601 date" while publishing them correctly, and was advised to add dates that were already there. It now reads the date property itself rather than a list of type names, which cannot go stale as schema.org adds subtypes. A date on a `WebSite` or `Organization` node still does not count, because that describes the site rather than the page.
